accuracy.evidence: Checked against CCSS RF.K.3a (one-to-one letter-sound correspondences, the primary sound for each consonant) and RF.K.3b (long and short sounds for the five major vowels), the EYFS 2024 ELG Word Reading (say a sound for each letter in the alphabet) and the England Year 1 programme of study (respond speedily with the correct sound to graphemes). Every keyword picture starts with its letter's most common sound (c as k in cat, s as sss in sun, f as fff in fish); the long vowel words go, me and hi really use the letter-name sound, and cake is only named as a long a in feedback, never taught as a single-letter spelling.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early phonics errors (Letters and Sounds DfES 2007 notes on pure sounds; Treiman and Kessler on letter-name interference): giving the letter name for the sound (prediction em vs mmm, cat-to-s feedback the name of c is see, challenge tag name), adding a schwa (tag uh: muh would make moon sound like muh-oon), b and d reversal (tag flip and the bus round), p and b voicing confusion (tag near), short e and short i (prediction on bed, tag ei), and short versus long vowels (tags short and long).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagphon is a letter-sound board: flip tiles that turn a letter into its sound and keyword picture, drop a picture on the letter for its initial sound, drop a vowel into the medial slot of a CVC frame, and sort words by short vowel or letter name. flagrime (onsets and rimes) splits words into onset and rime and flagsight is whole-word recognition, so no label swap could reuse this; the 30 percent shingle gate passed against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Flipping tiles shows the sound next to the name, so the child sees m is em but says mmm before being told; the first-sounds round makes the name strategy fail on cat (s is the letter named like see), the vowel round says the word the child actually built (c-u-t) so they hear why it is wrong, and the sort step contrasts dog and go with the same letter. Each done message states the rule only after the rounds.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: em for the sound of m (the flipped tile says mmm), sss like its name for c in cat (s is wrong, c says k), i for the middle of bed (the frame only makes bed with e), and o like octopus for go (go belongs in says its name). A.reveal repeats the child's guess in the done message.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with tagged wrong answers, each with its own correction: name (that is the letter's name, not its sound), uh (keep it pure, muh-oon), flip (b and d face different ways), near (p is a puff, bus starts with b), vowel (cot has o), long (in cake the a says its name), short (short o is in dog), first (that is not the middle vowel) and ei (e is egg, i is insect). Wrong drops in the lab name the slip too.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs are short read-aloud sentences (This is m. Its name is em. But in a word, m says mmm.) and validate_lessons passes the family kid limit; the adult text passes its limit while using the precise phonics terms grapheme, phoneme, grapheme-phoneme correspondence, consonant, short vowel, long vowel, initial sound, medial sound and CVC word.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed and overlap with every lesson, including Knowing all letters and Onsets and rimes, is under 12 percent. Each kid paragraph adds one idea (name versus sound, read with the sound, pure sounds, vowels short and long); the adult paragraphs give the standards, the key terms, four named mistakes with the reason they matter for blending, and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark: the six flip tiles fill two rows of three (about 110 by 90 px), the five vowel boxes fit one row at about 60 px each with letter, picture and keyword readable, the tray card is 116 by 72 px, and every action has a 56 px button twin under the canvas. Nothing is clipped; the long label ay, ee, eye, oh, you fits its box.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone 13, no console or page errors, all 5 Show me tasks completed and the challenge showed. Every drag has a labelled button (Starts with c, Middle e, Says its name), the canvas aria-label speaks each result (c says k, like cat), and correct and wrong states use a thick border plus words, not colour alone.
